abstract.t: A profile of RFC 7914's PBKDF2 test vectors for pbkdf2HmacSha256 in nish/crypto/hmac (std/crypto/hmac.ts). RFC 7914 defines scrypt; its Section 11 prints test vectors for PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256, the function scrypt is built on, and every one of them is held here.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

nish/crypto/hmac exports PBKDF2 with HMAC-SHA-256 as its pseudorandom function, over a password held as a Secret, a salt, an iteration count and a derived-key length. SCRAM-SHA-256's Hi is this function with a 32-byte output, which is how nish/net/postgres uses it.
RFC 7914 has no binding sentence in the sense of BCP 14 for PBKDF2, so the profile does not claim it as its main source: there is no completeness to check.

Section 11 prints both vectors, and vector 0.6.0 cannot cite either, so each takes its expected value from Python's hashlib, as a command spec check --run-sources runs; the bytes it prints are the ones Section 11 prints, byte for byte. Section 11 prints each value under the label PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 (P="passwd", S="salt", c=1, dkLen=64) =, split across two lines. vector asks for that label on the Expected value, and its Markdown literal grammar refuses one with a ", an = or a comma inside its parentheses ("Expected: not a literal"). The labels c and dkLen on the integer arguments are refused as well: vector reads them back from this profile's own Test Vectors section, finds c and dkLen on both rows, and refuses ("nothing pairs a printed string with one of several labelled values"). The integers are left bare, and spec check warns that each has no label to find it by.

section.name: Interface
section.sourcecode: // module: nish/crypto/hmac export const pbkdf2HmacSha256 = (password: Secret<u8[]>, salt: u8[], iterations: i32, length: i32): Secret<u8[]> | null

blockquote.t: The test vectors below can be used to verify the PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 [RFC2898] function.
The password and salt strings are passed as sequences of ASCII [RFC20] octets.

section.name: Laws
section.t: PBKDF2 computes its output block by block, each block from the password, the salt, the count and the block's index alone, so a shorter key is a prefix of a longer one under the same inputs. The vectors hold 64-byte keys; the clause below holds the lengths around SHA-256's 32-byte block.

front.title: The scrypt Password-Based Key Derivation Function

abstract.t: This document specifies the password-based key derivation function scrypt. The function derives one or more secret keys from a secret string. It is based on memory-hard functions, which offer added protection against attacks using custom hardware. The document also provides an ASN.1 schema.

front.title: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels

abstract.t: In many standards track documents several words are used to signify the requirements in the specification. These words are often capitalized. This document defines these words as they should be interpreted in IETF documents. This document specifies an Internet Best Current Practices for the Internet Community, and requests discussion and suggestions for improvements.

front.title: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words

abstract.t: RFC 2119 specifies common key words that may be used in protocol specifications. This document aims to reduce the ambiguity by clarifying that only UPPERCASE usage of the key words have the defined special meanings.
